indicators.note: things manufactured are made up anew, so the letters of the clue word are put together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Aircraft built by an Italian maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' rearranges PLANES into the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Naples is a large city found in southern Italy, so it is something located there.

clue.text: Shift of retirement is almost secure

parts.note: almost means nigh, as in nigh on

explanation.surface: Someone's change of job on retiring is nearly guaranteed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' looks like a work period, but it is a loose dress; 'retirement' means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a simple dress, and one worn when retiring for the night is bedwear.

parts.note: something laid down has lain, past participle of lie

explanation.surface: A man called Frank has had a royal put in his place.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a name, but it is the adjective meaning candid.

clue.text: Ostentatious cheer when wild boar is captured

explanation.surface: A hunting party celebrates as a wild boar is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The hunting picture hides the mechanics: 'wild' scrambles the animal and 'is captured' puts it inside the word for cheer; 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborate is showily detailed, close in sense to ostentatious display.

parts.note: busy at something means engaged in it

explanation.surface: A doubter who took part in a gun raid.

explanation.surface: A huntsman pursued for his labours over many years.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Actaeon saw Artemis bathing, was turned into a stag and hunted down by his own hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical huntsman became the quarry of his own dogs, so he was a hunter who was hunted.

clue.text: One aspiring to dance with the Queen

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to dance with the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aspiring to something hopes for it, so they are one who hopes.

clue.text: In dialect, translation is the same

indicators.note: a translation recasts the words, here rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A dialect phrase translates to the same meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges IN DIALECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical things match exactly, being one and the same.

parts.note: to hatch a scheme is to plan it

explanation.surface: The moment has come to design the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw or reed laid over a roof is a traditional roofing material.

indicators.note: the boy's name is placed in the abbreviation for school

indicators.note: the profits are placed in the butting animal

gains are profits

explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the spread but something that butts: a goat.

clue.text: Egyptian tucking into bread is a sorry subject for painting

parts.note: pita is a flatbread

explanation.surface: An Egyptian eating bread is a pitiful sight for an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating, but it means going inside.

clue.text: Rumpus about new work of art

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters in the words before it

explanation.definitionFit: A theoretic idea exists in theory rather than practice, so it is impractical.

clue.text: Point to a couple of trees showing rot

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
yew is one tree
ash is another tree

explanation.surface: Indicating a pair of trees that are decaying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rot' looks like decay, but it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is nonsense or humbug, a synonym for rot meaning rubbish talk.

parts.note: to log something is to enter it in a record
the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
taken as written

explanation.surface: Recording army reserves in a port.

explanation.definitionFit: To harbour an idea is to entertain it, holding it in mind.

parts.note: without means having no
vice covers bad habits

explanation.surface: A trainee free of bad habits.
explanation.walkthrough: A novice is also a trainee nun, so 'habits' plays on nuns' dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a beginner, someone in training.

indicators.note: the new lawyer is put in the case

parts.note: a valise is a small travelling case
a DA, district attorney, is an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A fresh attorney tears a case to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests a legal case beside 'lawyer', but it is a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: To vandalise something is to wreck or damage it wilfully.

clue.text: Pressure is beginning to smash lock

indicators.note: the start of the next word gives its first letter

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Pressure is starting to break a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door fitting, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is strain or pressure.

indicators.note: the son catches, takes inside, the breath

parts.note: a son is a descendant
wind means breath, as in getting one's wind back

explanation.surface: A son pauses to catch his breath at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Swindon is an English town in Wiltshire; 'here' points to the place the wordplay builds.
explanation.definitionFit: The wordplay names a town, and 'here' points to that very place.

parts.note: a rod stands for its user, a fisherman

explanation.surface: A fisherman out with his rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rod' stands for the person who holds one.
explanation.definitionFit: A wangler gets things by clever manoeuvring or scheming.

parts.note: to win something is to catch or get it
to try someone is to plague or vex them

explanation.surface: Coming down with a plague is grim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch plague' reads as falling ill; the words mean win and try.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintry weather is cold and cheerless, so bleak.

parts.note: RE, Royal Engineers, are British army soldiers
dead beat means exhausted

explanation.surface: Exhausted troops departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has retired has left work or withdrawn.

indicators.note: without means outside here, the drink wrapped round the sleep

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Snatch a drink when you can't sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but in its old sense means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap up a bargain is to grab it eagerly.

clue.text: People mobbing a bishop in Reading

indicators.note: the people crowd round the other pieces

parts.note: a nation is a people
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A crowd surrounds a bishop in the town of Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading looks like the English town, but it is a recital.
explanation.definitionFit: A narration is a telling of a story, like a reading aloud.

clue.text: A desire to be in company

parts.note: to long is to desire

explanation.surface: Wanting to be among people.
explanation.definitionFit: To come along is to come in company with someone, accompanying them.

parts.note: a bit restrains a horse

explanation.definitionFit: A bugle is a brass instrument used for military calls.

parts.note: ado is fuss

explanation.surface: A couple make a scene in a gallery.

explanation.definitionFit: The Prado is a famous gallery of paintings in Spain, an example of the type.

explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small pocket pistol.

indicators.note: the word for look goes into the colour

parts.note: bloodstained things are red
to see is to look
